_meta.title: Melanie — A Place for Mom (decision_helper archetype)
_meta.why_strong: Classic decision_helper archetype. The user (Mom) and the buyer (Melanie) are different people. Trigger event (father's death) is sharp. Emotional language signals overwhelm: 'would have given up or settled'.

persona.name: Adult-daughter Melanie, 51, suddenly-widowed mom needs a plan
persona.location_context: Chicago suburb, two kids in middle school, full-time job, mother lives 90 minutes away in Wisconsin
persona.primary_job: When my father suddenly died and Mom is in their empty house alone with no plan, I want to find an assisted living place near family, fast — without making the wrong choice and traumatizing her further.

pain_points.label: Knows nothing about senior living industry
pain_points.description: Has never researched assisted living before; doesn't know what types exist, what insurance covers, what to look for in a tour

pain_points.label: Caregiver guilt + grief overlap
pain_points.description: Just lost dad; doing rapid research with grief brain; feels guilty that she's even thinking about institutionalizing mom right after

pain_points.label: Geographic constraint with limited bandwidth
pain_points.description: Wants Mom near her own family in Chicago; can only tour places on weekends; can't take a week off work to visit a dozen communities

pain_points.label: Sibling friction
pain_points.description: Brother in California thinks Mom should stay in her own house with a part-time aide; not aligned on cost or urgency

trust_needs: Real person to call who knows the local market and isn't a salesperson on commission
Pre-vetted shortlist (not '47 communities to choose from')
Actual reviews from families who placed a parent recently
Clear pricing with no surprise fees
decision_triggers: Phone call with a real local advisor within 24 hours
Curated shortlist of 3 places matching budget + geo, ready by next weekend
Tour scheduling done for her, not by her
objections: Brother will say I'm rushing this and didn't try hard enough
What if Mom hates it and we have to move her again?
Is this 'free service' actually free or am I being upsold somewhere?
persona.channel_behavior: Mobile during commute and lunch break; desktop late evening after kids in bed; opens emails immediately but doesn't always reply

verbatim_quotes: Without them, I probably would have given up or settled.
I just don't have time to figure this out from scratch right now.
My brother thinks I'm overreacting but he's not the one driving up there every weekend.
